title: Developmental Trauma: The Hidden Epidemic
coreMove: Treat chronic childhood trauma as a developmental injury: name the pattern, coordinate the adults, and make safety and prevention the aim before punishment.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ellie, a school coordinator translating behavior into safety questions
exampleSpecs.stakes: A student may be suspended before any adult asks what danger trained the reaction.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the National Child Traumatic Stress Network to widen the adult response.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rahul, a clinic supervisor catching a pattern behind separate labels
exampleSpecs.stakes: The intake team may medicate separate symptoms while missing chronic caregiver trauma.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show why the DSM proposal mattered despite rejection.

exampleSpecs.audience: Emile, a probation liaison linking court orders to trauma care
exampleSpecs.stakes: A court order may raise control without changing the danger that shaped the behavior.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show why child trauma cannot be handled by psychotherapy alone.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ava, a policy aide connecting prevention spending to childhood trauma
exampleSpecs.stakes: A budget hearing may treat trauma only as a clinic expense after harm has occurred.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use European prevention contrasts to connect policy with trauma risk.

exampleSpecs.audience: Jade, a caseworker stopping a handoff from becoming another rupture
exampleSpecs.stakes: A placement crisis may be read as bad behavior instead of fear of another loss.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show foster parents and professionals sharing one trauma frame.

exampleSpecs.audience: Lily, a pediatric nurse defending a developmental formulation
exampleSpecs.stakes: A medical team may treat DSM rejection as a reason to drop the broader trauma pattern.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show why rejection of the proposed diagnosis did not erase the clinical pattern.
